definitions.explanation: The finger between the thumb and the middle finger, used for pointing. Called the "person-pointing finger" in Japanese.

examples.japanese: {人差|ひとさ}し{指|ゆび}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{画面|がめん}→画面：04406_gamen⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦タッチ→タッチ：08915_tacchi⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: Touch the screen with your index finger.

examples.japanese: {人差|ひとさ}し{指|ゆび}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{口|くち}→口：00560_kuchi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{当|あ}てて→当てる：01864_ateru⟧「しっ」⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{言|い}った→言う：00515_iu⟧。
examples.english: She put her index finger to her lips and said "shh."

examples.japanese: ⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{人差|ひとさ}し{指|ゆび}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{指|さ}す→指す：02056_sasu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{失礼|しつれい}→失礼：01247_shitsurei⟧だ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{言|い}われている→言う：00515_iu⟧。
examples.english: It's said to be rude to point at people with your index finger.

notes:
The index finger, used for pointing. In Japanese culture, pointing at people with this finger is considered rude.

ETYMOLOGY:
Literally "person-pointing finger" — ⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧ (person) + ⟦{差|さ}す→差す：17637_sasu⟧ (to point) + ⟦{指|ゆび}→指：01518_yubi⟧ (finger). Named for its role in pointing at people.

ALL FIVE FINGERS:
- ⟦{親指|おやゆび}→親指：04114_oyayubi⟧: thumb ("parent finger")
- {人差|ひとさ}し{指|ゆび}: index finger ("person-pointing finger")
- ⟦{中指|なかゆび}→中指：04281_nakayubi⟧: middle finger ("middle finger")
- ⟦{薬指|くすりゆび}→薬指：16373_kusuriyubi⟧: ring finger ("medicine finger")
- ⟦{小指|こゆび}→小指：04029_koyubi⟧: little finger, pinky ("small finger")

CULTURAL NOTE:
Pointing at people with the {人差|ひとさ}し{指|ゆび} is considered impolite in Japan. When indicating a person or direction, Japanese people often gesture with an open hand instead.
